proposed_widenings.name: passive_advancement
proposed_widenings.justification: Class features that are granted permanently at a given level (no activation, no resource, no reset) have no mechanics family in the surface. All existing ClassFeatureMechanics share the 'activation' family which mandates activationCost, resource, and resetCadence — none of which apply to a level-up permanent grant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see 'Feats') or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat
proposed_widenings.justification: The effect of this feature is gaining a feat permanently. No effect atom in v4 captures feat grants. The closest candidate (grant_proficiency) models a proficiency bonus, not a full feat with its own mechanics. A feat grant opens a player-choice over a scoped feat category (Epic Boon feats) or any qualifying feat.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see 'Feats') or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Truesight is recommended.

proposed_widenings.name: feat_category_choice (FeatScope variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: The feat selection is scoped to a category ('Epic Boon feat') with an open fallback ('or another feat of your choice for which you qualify'). The surface has no type for a player-resolved choice over a feat category. This is a distinct selection grammar from the existing TargetSelection (which selects creatures).
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see 'Feats') or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

notes: This is the same structural gap as Ability Score Improvement and all other level-up passive grants. The surface models activated class features (Action Surge, Second Wind) but has no family for features that are permanent character-advancement grants received at level-up with no combat runtime footprint. The 'activation' family is the only ClassFeatureMechanics variant and it cannot be coerced into representing a passive permanent feat grant without lying about the structure.
